utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I understand that before the witness comes in, there's a matter that you wish to raise, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Yes, I would like to inform the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution of our intentions in the further leading of our case. As you have noted, and I believe that the Prosecution has already observed this, there was no notification yesterday for our upcoming witnesses, for the witnesses two weeks from now. In our prior notification, we notified the five witnesses, and the Trial Chamber approved one of those witnesses to testify via videolink, I believe, after the 12th of -- the week of the 12th of May, but we are now faced with a problem in finding the right time for an expert witness who dealt with the problems of the role of the chief of the security -- state security department. We have been unable so far to establish a time when he would be able to appear. As things stand now, that is either going to be in the week of the 10th or the 17th of May, but I cannot actually confirm either date. What I can say is that the remaining witnesses on that list will not be called by the Defence. We have decided not to call them. And I believe both the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution need to be informed of this because of further Scheduling Orders and arrangements. And if the Trial Chamber wants me to tell you, I can name the witnesses that will not be called by the Defence, or do you feel that it's sufficient that what I've already said so far, namely the witnesses who will appear is sufficient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, just to be certain in our minds, I see your intension after the present witness to call Mr. Stalevic, Mr. Misic, Mr. Cankovic. Beyond that, your expert. Is there somebody else that you will be calling?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. The videolink witness, Spasic, will be testifying. And you've named all the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what you are advising is that beyond the witnesses that I have read off from your notifications of witnesses for the week of the 19th and the 26th, and the witness Spasic, you will not be calling any other witness on the list, the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me be even more specific. I only meant the witnesses who were on the list. We've also submitted a request to the Trial Chamber to reconsider your decision regarding the expert Pavic, so that witness will depend on the Trial Chamber's decision. And as for the other witnesses, we propose to tender via bar table their statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you have in mind there, but let's take this at one step at a time. After the present witness, Stalevic, Misic, Cankovic, Spasic, and your motion about Pavic is to be determined. Are they the witnesses whom you now intend to call?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I misspoke. What I meant was that I would submit evidence via bar table. So we have Mr. Simovic who is testifying now, then we have Stalevic, Misic, Cankovic, Pasic. Our expert witness, Mr. Milasinovic, and depending on the Trial Chamber's decision on our motion, we'll also have the expert witness Mr. Pavic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. And there could be an expectation that apart from the expert Spasic, or sorry, the ill man Spasic and Milasinovic, all the others will be called this week or next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have another request, namely, yes, we plan all of these witnesses to be heard by the end of the week, provided that the air traffic returns to normal. As things stand now, one of these witnesses is supposed to appear on Thursday. As for the other one, we don't know when he will show up, but we hope that he can be brought in as well, but we would appreciate if we could start their testimony, their questioning next week because we are not sure how much time we will have to proof them. But as -- from what we what we know now, they cannot -- neither of them will be here before Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are speaking there of Misic and Cankovic, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. At the moment then, either this week or next week, we will complete the evidence of those witnesses, leaving just Spasic, Milasinovic, and the question mark of the motion concerning Pavic. Is that correct? Clearly, it would be desirable to hear both Spasic and Milasinovic in the one week. It would be more efficient use of everybody's time and of this courtroom if that could be done. So if you could concentrate your efforts on trying to get those two witnesses to be available to be dealt with in the one week. It's not so critical at this point which of the two weeks you've mentioned that will be as long as they are both able to be heard in the one week, if that can be arranged. I would expect that in the course of this week you will have a decision concerning Mr. Pavic and you will be able to take steps accordingly depending on the outcome of that decision. Is there any observation, Mr. Stamp, that you feel you need to make at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I first would like to express my gratitude to counsel for informing us of the anticipated schedule at this stage. It will assist us in making our own plans. The first issue is the -- in respect to the witnesses Misic and Cankovic. Can I take it that the Court has accepted the request of the Defence that they not start, none of them start this week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have yet to consult the two other members of the Court on this. I was trying to get clear what it is we need to look at before we consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. That will have something to do with how we relocate our sources between now and next week. The other thing is a matter that I was considering raising before, it's a housekeeping matter. Since we now know that the case for the Defence will probably close on the week beginning the 10th or the next week, I was wondering, and it's really a matter for the Court, if a Scheduling Order could issue in respect to our considerations of applications for rebuttal evidence, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have such applications?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We are considering it, and I could indicate to the Court that our anticipation is that there will be none, but we still have it open. We are considering persons, but we have to make a final decision based on any schedule the Court makes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will understand from the point of view of the Chamber unless there's a motion, there's nothing for us to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I was wondering if an order as to the latest when such a motion could be filed could be issued, because we want to consider it on the basis of all the evidence we hear. I just could indicate now, we don't anticipate to file with respect to the three or so witnesses we are thinking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are these affected by the evidence of Spasic, Milasinovic, or Pavic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They will probably be affected by the evidence of Misic and Milasinovic. I do not want to say too much, Your Honour, because we have not made a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying you cannot make a decision until those witnesses have given their evidence, or are you able to make a decision in light of your expectations about the evidence of Spasic and Milasinovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A decision could be made before these persons testify, but it would be more convenient to the Prosecution if we hear them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point is one of expedition and delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I know, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because if it is that you do move to hear rebuttal evidence and if your arguments were persuasive and you were to call it, clearly we would want to move on quickly to that evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it's the position that there's no consideration of that issue until after you file a motion after the evidence of Spasic and Milasinovic is heard, we could well be into June before we come to hear any rebuttal evidence, if that is the course which is to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, that is a why I raise it because now I understand it seems to me that the Court's position is that the earlier any such motion is filed, the better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. And one consideration, of course, is the availability, if at all, we move the Court in this regard, the availability of the witnesses. We have only spoken to one person to put that witness on standby. But I could take it then, subject to the Court's consideration, that we -- the earlier the better. The next issue before the Court considers anything is re-opening of the Prosecution's case to call one witness. There was an issue in respect to K-87 who had the serious medical problems. We received a medical report this week, I think it's yesterday or probably this morning, indicating that he is able to testify, but not to travel. I have not seen the report, I have not been able to consult with the doctors or the persons who are reviewing it, but it may well be that the Prosecution may want to move that the case be re-opened just to take in his evidence formal and give the Defence an opportunity to cross-examine him by videolink in the same week as their application. I just inform the Court of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The evidence of Mr. -- at the same time as the evidence of Mr. Spasic; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The same week, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They would both be from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand that the medical report is that he should not travel but he could testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We, of course, have not seen any such medical report at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It will be filed as soon as possible this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber would indicate that first we thank you, Mr. Djurdjic, for your raising of this matter at this stage, which is a very convenient stage for planning purposes. We accept that because of the difficulties at the moment of air travel, that the evidence of Mr. Misic and Cankovic should be heard next week, rather than this week, so we will hear the present witness and Mr. Stalevic this week, and then adjourn, assuming we finish before the end of the week, to resume on Monday of next week for the evidence of Mr. Misic and Cankovic. That will leave, then, the evidence of Mr. Pavic to be determined according to a decision, which I believe we can expect this week. Leaving Mr. Pavic aside, that will leave the witness Mr. Spasic and the witness Milasinovic, clearly if those two can be heard in the one week, one is by videolink and one is not, it would be much more practical for court use and for the attendance of counsel and convenience. And we would leave it with you, Mr. Djurdjic, subject to a matter I'll mention in a moment, to resolve whether that can be arranged for the week commencing the 10th of May, or failing that, the week commencing the 17th of May. The Prosecution has raised two matters. First, whether there should be leave to lead rebuttal evidence or whether there will be a motion for leave. And the second is whether there should be a recalling of the witness K-87, who although called earlier was not in a state of health to attend, and his evidence was received by way of statement. In the Chamber's view, Mr. Stamp, it would be practical if by Friday, I think it's the 30th of April, that is the end of next week -- that's the holiday. By Thursday the 29th of April, you just lost a day, Mr. Stamp, the -- any motion that the Prosecution may consider it should bring, if any, with a view to re-opening your case, or with a view to calling rebuttal evidence should be filed. If that is done, we would allow the Defence a week in which to respond, if it wishes to that. That would take us to the end of the first week of May, and the Chamber will then be -- to the Thursday evening at the end of the first week of May. That will then enable the Chamber to consider whether any motion that is moved by the Prosecution should or should not be granted. We would draw attention to the fact that if a videolink is to be organised for Mr. Spasic, and if it is that K-87 is to be called by way of videolink, it clearly would be, again, in the practical interest of everybody if those could be arranged either on the same day or on successive days from Belgrade. And the Chamber would certainly try to facilitate that. But that will require some liaison between Prosecution and Defence, as well as some speedy attention to these motions, if it is to be the case that K-87 is to be recalled and if he is to give evidence at about the same time as Mr. Spasic by videolink from Belgrade. Having, therefore, posed this possible outcome of what we've been talking about today, can we leave it initially with counsel for the Prosecution and the Defence to discuss whether there is a date that would be convenient to both for the purposes of videolink from Belgrade, if it is that K-87 is to be called by way of videolink. Now, we don't know he whether there will be a motion for him to be called either by Prosecution or given the terms of our decision about him, it could be a motion by the Defence. But if there is to be a motion for him to be recalled to actually give oral evidence and if that is to be by videolink, it's clearly an opportunity not to be missed for him to give evidence at the same time, give or take a day, as Mr. Spasic. Discussion with the Chamber's Legal Officer is urged at any time if in the course of the discussions between counsel it appears that we are headed toward calling both Mr. Spasic and K-87 by videolink so that we can make appropriate orders and get administrative arrangements into place. And if that should happen, that will be either the week of the 10th of May, or the week of the 17th of May, depending on the arrangements that Mr. Djurdjic will initially be making concerning the witness Spasic and the witness who will give evidence here, Milasinovic. Have we left enough guidance to counsel for these matters to be pursued in an orderly fashion? We hope so. We don't want to be too prescriptive. Counsel in this case have been very good at discussing issues and reaching practical outcome, we think it convenient to leave this matter on that basis for the moment. Thank you for that. We, therefore, can look forward to close of Defence evidence either by the end of the week of the 10th or the end of the week of the 17th of May. And it may be that there could be some Prosecution evidence to follow, but the Chamber would hope that if that is to be the case, that that can be immediately following the evidence of the witnesses we have mentioned so that we can be well clear of all evidence by the end of May. We thank counsel for that useful discussion, and if there's nothing else we should have the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Simovic. Our apologies for keeping you waiting. We had matters that had to be dealt with, but we are now back in normal session for the continuation of your evidence. If you could please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I remind you the affirmation you made to tell the truth continues to apply today. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Simovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could proceed where we left off yesterday and return to the document 65 ter 6118, and while it's brought up, I'd like to just read to you what you said yesterday. And this is at page 13619, lines 4 to 9: "These reservists" -- this is a question. "The reservists at the time when you escorted them to Podujevo they were under your command, were they not?" Your answer is: "Not yet. I had only taken them over." "Q. So when you say you took them over, can I take it that it means that you were responsible for giving them orders?" And you said: "No."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So if we could go back to this document and the same place we were yesterday, it's at the bottom of the page in English, about line 12 on the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the penultimate sentence of that page in English, the Judge recorded you as saying, and this in Prokuplje: "This is why I immediately called the commander of the Skorpions, Slobodan Medic and ordered him to gather his unit and return to Prolom Banja." The first question is: Did you say that to the magistrate or to the investigating -- to the trial judges, actually, at the Prokuplje district court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, just for the record let's start. The part I read you from the court record, and I'll reread it again, and the question is: "Did you say this?" "I immediately called the commander of the Skorpions, Slobodan Medic, and ordered him to gather his unit and return to Prolom Banja." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't say that the commander was Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you say that you ordered him, Slobodan Medic, to gather his unit and return to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You are insisting on the fact that this is Medic's units. I said it was the reserve composition of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia and that the commander Trajkovic had just told me that the contact was Medic. That is to say that that was the man he talked to and in a way told him that he would be in charge of them. He wasn't their commander. They were still under the command of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia because they were reserve force of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, and that's why I've been saying this all the time non-stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you tell the Judges in Prokuplje that you ordered Medic to gather his unit and return to Prolom Banja? That is the question. Simply, did you tell the Judges that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I ordered Medic, not Commander Medic. You are insisting on saying Commander Medic. I ordered Medic, but not Commander Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. You still seem not to understand the question. I just want to get your answer as to whether or not the judges made a proper and accurate record. So before I come to the truth of your comments, can you just tell us if this record is accurate? Did you say: "I immediately called the commander of the Skorpions, Slobodan Medic, and ordered him to gather his unit and return to Prolom Banja?"

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say again, I said I ordered Medic. Not Commander Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Who was the commander of this group of men that you took over in Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were the reserve force of the MUP, and nobody had taken them over yet, so I'm stating once again that it was only Commander Trajkovic who orally talked to Medic and told him to be in charge of them until they were taken over by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I just read the record to you. You said yesterday: "I had only taken them over." This is at 13619 at line 6. Didn't you testify yesterday actually on more than one occasion that you went to Prolom Banja and took them over?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You don't understand. I went to fetch them, but I didn't take them over as a unit. I could have taken them over as a unit only at the point in time when they were attached to my own unit and when I report to the staff that they had been joined to the unit. They had not been attached to the unit. I brought them in as the reserve force and returned them as members of the reserve force, and please allow me to finish my sentence. Don't interrupt me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are not answering my question, and, Mr. Simovic, you are not here just to speak whatever you want to say. Just answer the questions. You told us yesterday on more than one occasion, and I read the record again, you are asked: "These reservists at the time when you escorted them to Podujevo they were under your command, were they not?" And you said: "Not yet. I had only taken them over." Is that evidence which you gave yesterday not correct? Is it not true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that they weren't under my command, and that is my final answer. They were not under my command. They were the reserve force of the MUP, and I'm trying to explain this to you. If they were to come under the -- I'm trying to explain when they came under the SAJ command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am aware of that, but I'm also aware that you are in a point of some significance on this issue, and I was waiting until you had asked your question and got your answer before turning to Mr. Djurdjic. Is there more you are going to ask about this? It's not -- very well, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two points. Why I'm on my feet is the primary point. I think the witness is trying to answer and respond but that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, sorry, I don't want you to start interpreting his evidence. If there's a point of difficulty about translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I won't. That's all I wanted to say. I think that he answered the question, but I think the Trial Chamber and I understand each other. Now, with respect to the interpretation and translation in the text read out by Mr. Stamp, it says, the word is "nalozia," that is to say, instructed. Is there this nuance between instruction and order? "nalozia" is to instruct, "narediti" is to order; whereas, we keep getting a different interpretation. So that's the distinct I wish to make and to state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There's evidence before the Court -- or let me just put this in the form of a question. Did you know whether or not these so-called reservists that you picked up at Prolom Banja or took over at Prolom Banja had a commander amongst them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They could not have a commander because they were the reserve force of the MUP. Reservists cannot ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your answer is you don't know.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, my answer is that they don't have one and cannot have one because they are the reserve force of the MUP. A reserve MUP force cannot have a commander because in the reserve force you can never take a unit, just an individual as a physical entity. Do you understand me? Whereas you keep insisting on me telling you what you want to hear, that it's a unit. It's not a unit, and they haven't got a commander, and they are the reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is a great deal of background noise and it's very difficult to hear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I keep insisting because I have here a record from a district court in a murder trial of your evidence, and I keep asking you whether you said something and you keep refusing to answer, that's all. So I'll ask it one last time. Did you tell the Court that you call the commander of the Skorpions Slobodan Medic? Either you told them or you didn't tell them that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's not that I called them. I just told Mr. Medic and from Commander Trajkovic he was in charge of them --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, you refuse to answer my question. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not refusing to answer. You are not accepting the answer I'm giving you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was it not your duty, Mr. Simovic, to gather the evidence in respect to the massacre, to the murders that had been committed at Podujevo that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I said yesterday that in my unit I did not have any experts who would conduct an investigation --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed the OUP of Podujevo who -- which was in charge of that. That is to take steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I take it then that your answer is that you -- your view is that you had no responsibility to gather any evidence? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My answer is this: I undertook everything in order to ensure that proceedings be undertaken to arrive at the perpetrators of the crime. First of all, on site I asked people if anybody had seen anybody shooting. The answer I received was no. I could not just at random select somebody who did the shooting, so I informed the organ in charge of that to conduct an investigation, an on-site investigation, to uncover the perpetrators of the crime, and those perpetrators were indeed uncovered and brought to justice in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this is the last time I'm going to ask you the same question again. Did you consider that you had a responsibility on the spot to gather evidence in respect to this crime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Everything that was in my power I undertook. That is to say, I undertook what I could immediately, which was to report the case to the competent authorities so that they could initiate further steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you the most senior MUP personnel on the scene at the time when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not an official of MUP. At the time, I was the commander of my own unit of the SAJ, and as on the spot, there was the reserve force and my unit. As far as my unit is concerned, I had the highest rank. But there were others, other members of the regular police, the army, in the vicinity. So I don't know whether there was anybody of higher rank there or not. As far as my SAJ unit, I was the commander and, therefore, highest in rank at that given point in time, only in the SAJ. I can't speak for other units because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I put the question this way: As far as you knew and at the time you arrived at the scene of this murder, mass murder, you were the most senior policeman there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of my members, yes, but only my members. Now, I don't know whether 50 metres away there might have been a colonel of the regular police, for example. But for my unit, I had the highest rank, as far as my unit was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are saying it's possible a colonel of the police might have been on the scene of that murder and you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say on the scene, on the scene of the crime. 50 or 100 metres away is not on site. I'm talking about on site and among my unit members I was -- had the highest rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look on this record we see a statement I read to you yesterday, and I'd just like to get your answer for the record, so please listen to the question and give me a direct answer so I could move on. The record of the court is that you said: "I did not enter the area where the civilians were killed because professional medical care was being provided there." The question is, did you tell the Court that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this point in time I cannot remember whether I said that to the Court or not. If that's what it says there, then most probably that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know whether any medical attention was provided to anybody inside the courtyard where these persons were shot?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by medical attention. That could be taking someone's temperature. If you are asking about first aid to those who were injured, the first aid was provided, and when I arrived on site, I saw Dr. Dragan administering professional medical assistance to the injured persons, but I cannot say with certainty whether this was happening in the courtyard or on the side of the road, and that is what I said yesterday, and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I get back to the question ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to waste anyone's time, but I believe we are still here at the same problem where we left off yesterday. I've been trying to read the portion of the court records, and I can't see where any reference is made to the courtyard. I don't see that the witness said that he mentioned the courtyard anywhere because we keep getting this term "courtyard" in our translation. So I would appreciate if Mr. Stamp could tell us what line is it where this word "courtyard" is mentioned in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last two questions I asked in reference to the courtyard was not about the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp quoted his statement and mentioned the courtyard, and he was trying to point out the contradictions in his statement when compared to the court records of those proceedings, so could Mr. Stamp please tell us exactly what it is that he is quoting when he is putting a question to the witness, and that should help both me and the Trial Chamber to know exactly which portion he is referring to and then I wouldn't have to stand up -- be up on my feet all the time to interfere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That matter was dealt with often yesterday in the transcript both in questions from Mr. Stamp and in quoting from the transcript of the Serbian court proceedings. And "courtyard" was mentioned in the course of that several times, Mr. Djurdjic. So you might care to either look again at the transcript or at yesterday's record and you will find the answers to your questions. Carry on, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, Mr. Simovic, now I'm moving off this document temporarily and asking you now a more general question. And it's simply this: Do you know whether any type of medical assistance, whether first aid, triage, or whatever, any type of medical assistance was provided to anybody in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All the injured were provided medical assistance. First aid. When I arrived there, I cannot say with certainty whether what I saw was happening in the courtyard or on the side of the road, but I am saying that everyone who needed professional medical assistance was provided assistance and then transported to Pristina where they were further treated and the best professional care was provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I suggest to you that you participated in a coverup of this gross crime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can state with full responsibility before this Trial Chamber that I did not take part in covering up any crime because the minute I found out about this incident, I informed the competent authorities in Podujevo and the staff, and the competent organs then took all the investigative measures required. So I claim with full responsibility that I did not even try, let alone cover up any crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You say the competent authorities took all the necessary measures. On what basis do you say or did you become aware that the competent authorities took all the necessary measures?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say that because I informed the Podujevo OUP which had the territorial jurisdiction for that area, and then I informed the Podujevo -- the Podujevo staff informed the investigating judge, which was within their competence, who then undertook investigative measures as provided for their service.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you check at any time to see that the measures taken by the Podujevo OUP or by the investigating judge at that time when the massacre was committed were, in fact, adequate? And I ask that question because you say that the competent authorities took all measures. Did you check to ensure that they did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They had to do it ex officio.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I take it that although you haven't answered the question I asked, your answer really is that you did not, but you assume that they did ex officio?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they were duty-bound to do that ex officio. They were duty-bound.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, can you just answer my question. Did you, as a senior, I put it the senior police officer coming on the scene of that massacre, did you check to ensure that they took all the necessary measures? Can you answer that question directly, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The measures had to be taken ex officio, but I already said yesterday before this Court that after informing the Podujevo OUP and the staff and the chief of department, I set off for Belgrade, so at the time when I was leaving the territory of Podujevo, that was the time when the investigative measures would have been undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But I think you agreed with me that when you left Podujevo, no investigating judge and no prosecutor arrived.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us yesterday, I think, that you did not know approximately how many were killed on the day in question, and I think you said it's because you did not look into the courtyard to count. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know on that same day how many victims there were in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That day did you tell anybody that there were more than a dozen killed? A dozen civilians killed, more than a dozen civilians killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I reported to the Podujevo OUP of the incident. I informed the staff and the chief of the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Focus on the question I asked, please. Did you tell anybody that day that more than a dozen civilians were killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the chief of the Podujevo OUP was there so he would have to take all the measures. In other words, if I informed the Podujevo OUP, that means that I did inform someone, but I can't recall exactly by name who it was, but when you report an incident, you report it to the competent authorities who then have to take all the necessary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I ask you a third time but more precisely this time, and please answer the question. Did you report to Mr. Djordjevic that more than a dozen civilians had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I informed the Podujevo OUP and the staff on the measures that I was taking to return --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- the reserve force, I called the chief -- please, I am trying to answer your question. So when I informed why I was returning these men, I also told them why it was that I wanted them sent back because the MUP reservists had fired at civilians and that was the reason why I wanted to send them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, did you on that day report to Mr. Djordjevic that more than a dozen people had been killed by -- or simply, just did you report to Mr. Djordjevic that more than a dozen people had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed Mr. Djordjevic of the reasons why I was sending these men back, in other words, that they had fired at civilians. But I don't recall that I mentioned the number of victims or even -- or even a random number of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, on the day of this incident at the time when you made your report to Mr. Djordjevic, were you aware that more than a dozen civilians had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was aware that civilians had been killed, but I was not aware of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Djordjevic told us that you told him that. Do you have any reason to doubt that evidence? That you, in fact, told him that more than a dozen had been killed? This is 9703.20 of the record. The question is, do you have any reason to doubt Mr. Djordjevic's evidence that you told him that more than a dozen had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can say and stand by only the statement that I provide myself. I stand by what I've already said that I did inform them of the incident, but I don't know that I mentioned the number of fatalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm going to just ask you to explain something to the Court, how it is that you were aware that this massacre had occurred? You had policemen under your command on the scene helping, as you say, and you did not find out how many people were killed that day. You went to the scene, your policemen were there. You said that you for whatever reason you did not look into the courtyard to count, but your men were there. How is it that you did not find out how many people were killed by the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not find out on the site how many fatalities there were, the fatalities in the aftermath of what the reservists of the Serbian MUP committed because I did not have any experts in my unit who could conduct an on-site investigation, and they could only do more harm than good. That is why we could not establish who had committed it, but we informed the OUP so that they could take professional measures, collect the evidence, and uncover the perpetrators of the crime and bring them to justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are not really answering the question. I'll ask it one more time. If you don't answer, I'll move on, but please try to answer. Your men were on the scene, and I remind you the doctor, the physician for the SAJ was on the scene. You were on the scene, the senior policeman, at least amongst your men. How is it that you did not know how many people were killed that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already answered your question a minute ago. In other words, I did not have professional officers in my unit who could conduct an investigation. I said that whatever they might have done could have been more harmful than beneficial. They would have had to be professional people who would take the evidence, collect the evidence there, and conduct an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could bring back 06118. And this is a record of your evidence at the first trial in Prokuplje. We could go to the same place where we were in B/C/S, and on the bottom in English. And we could remain on this page in English, but I'll read the last sentence that's down at the bottom and move on to the next page in English. The record says that you stated: "On the same day, practically immediately after this, I had to go to Belgrade for the funeral of Aleksic Radovan, a member of my unit who had been killed, so I did not conduct any further investigation at the scene. Anyway, the case was officially taken over by the local police, and they were to establish who had committed these murders. Precisely on the day when this incident happened, as I have already mentioned, I had to go to the funeral of one of the members of my unit, but he was not just an ordinary member of my unit. He was a man to whom I owed so much ..." And later on, and this is on the same page in B/C/S you said: "For the third or fourth time now, the Court insists that I give my final opinion about who or whose member fired at the civilians. I must repeat again what really happened, which is that on that day I was in a particularly difficult psychological state." Do you recall saying all of what I just read, or?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I've been reading it for myself as well, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you say what is in the record?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me just read it through. Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you see here from this record that the Court was insisting, as I insist in asking the question, that as a senior man, senior policeman present, you should have had more to offer to tell them about this massacre of women and children. You were there on the shortly after it happened. And the explanation you gave the Court for leaving was to attend the funeral of your friend. Was that evidence, Mr. Simovic, untrue? Your friend was not buried on the 28th. There was no funeral on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'll say it again. Before I left Prokuplje -- Podujevo rather, I did everything that I could. In other words, I informed the competent authorities, I informed the staff, and the chief of department and only then I set off for Belgrade. Now, you were asking me whether I had to go to Belgrade. I had to go to Belgrade. I had to go there and stand next to the body of one my members, and now you are actually insulting me here by sort of feeling that I shouldn't have been present at this funeral of one of my members.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not insulting you. I take the same attitude as the Court, that you need to explain what you were doing as a senior policeman present at the scene of a massacre committed by so-called reserve policemen. And my attitude is no different from the attitude of the Court in Prokuplje. The question is this, I repeat: There was no funeral of your friend on that day; isn't that correct? He was not buried on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day the remains -- his remains were supposed to arrive in Belgrade. Now, when you have the remains, they lie in state, and we provide the honour guard and I was supposed to be one of the members of that honour guard. Now, I repeat it again, I had to be in Belgrade on the 28th because one of my members had died. Even when your pet dies, the whole household is in sorrow let alone when one of your members, one of the members of your unit dies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What you told the Court here on more than one occasion that you left the scene to attend your friend's funeral is not true. And that's a simple question. There was no funeral on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After taking all the measures that I could, in other words, when I took all the measures that were within my powers, I left Podujevo and went to Belgrade. I could not exert any kind of influence over the pathologist as to when they would conduct their forensic investigation and when the late Aleksic would be transferred to Belgrade, but we all thought that this would be on the 28th so I had to be there. And even if his remains had not been already brought to Belgrade, we had to see and visit their family, his wife, his children. We had to inform his parents that they no longer had a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I think you testified before that Mr. Trajkovic had gone to Belgrade to do that, to make those arrangements. Is that so? Mr. Trajkovic made arrangements in respect to Mr. Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovic left on the 27th to make those arrangements, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, that's all.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But you had to provide, to find a grave and of course Trajkovic could not on my behalf express his condolences to his wife, his children, his mother and his sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anyway --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And he could not be with them at their most difficult hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, let's get back to the point though, and my point is that what you told the Court in order to explain why you did no investigations, that you left to go to a funeral of your dear friend is not true. So I'll just ask the question this way: What was the date of the funeral?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I do not recall exactly whether it was on the 29th or the 30th. In other words, I cannot recall the exact date, whether it was on the 29th or the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And when you told the Court in Prokuplje that you didn't do an investigation because you were leaving to go to a funeral on the 28th, you'll agree with me that that was not true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not an investigating judge. I am a police officer. I informed the authorities to take all the measures in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think we have to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we move on to another document. This is 06119.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, you recall that you were interviewed in respect to the events of the 28th of March, 1999, on the 15th of February, 2002 by a Working Group of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall that, Mr. Simovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember the date when the Working Group interviewed me, but at the time I did give an interview for three hours. Where it says here just five minutes of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, we are at the last page. Did you sign this record of this interview?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can I take it that you read the record before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, as a senior police officer, are you in the habit of signing statements in murder investigations without reading them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You don't know the circumstances under which this statement was taken, that's why you say that. It was a Working Group, I don't know how many of them. I can't remember whether I read this document before I signed it, but I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, it's only two pages long in Serbian. Is it possible that you might have signed this without reading it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This interview lasted for three hours, roughly three hours. And the Working Group dictated, typed so, no, I really don't know whether I actually read it, but as I say, I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This interview was conducted at your office, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't see where it was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember maybe?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It says here in the official premises of the gendarmerie command, but it wasn't in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That was at that time in 2002 February, the 15th of February, 2002, where your office was located; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Under that roof, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go to the third paragraph of the statement on the first page in the B/C/S and on the second page in the translation. You have to scroll down in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are recorded here as having said that while you were in a meeting, while the meeting was in progress, "I heard two bursts of automatic fire and rushed outside to see what was going on. About 500 metres from the Podujevo OUP, I came across members of the SAJ. Among them was Spasoje Vulevic, also known as Vuk, commander of the SAJ platoon Belgrade, who was holding one member of the Skorpion unit and shouting 'what have you done, fool?'" Did you say this in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember saying this, but I say with full responsibility that the member Vulevic, Spasoje saw who did the shooting to arrest him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When did you become aware that Spasoje saw who did the shooting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I arrived on the spot and when I encountered a group of my members giving assistance to the wounded, and while Dr. Dragan was doing that, Vulevic, my commanding officer of the 3rd Platoon said, Boss, members of the third composition were shooting at the civilians, the ones that were supposed to be in the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you see him holding on to one of them saying, according to this statement, "what have you done, fool?"

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you are saying now contrary to, I believe, what you were saying yesterday, that Spasoje saw who did the shooting to arrest them, and you said that with full responsibility today. Did you cause Spasoje to give a statement that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the spot Vulevic, and I repeat this once again, and not only Vulevic, but any of my members of the regular SAJ, the active members of the SAJ unit, had they seen anybody shooting, they would have arrested them. That's what I said yesterday and that's what I am repeating today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. What I have here on the record at line 16 of page 31 is: "I say with full responsibility that the member Vulevic, Spasoje saw who did the shooting to arrest him." Is that what you said or what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That Vulevic or had Vulevic saw -- had Vulevic saw somebody shooting, he would certainly have arrested him. Had he seen that. So any active member of the SAJ and authorised person belonging to the SAJ, had they seen somebody using fire-arms and shooting at civilians, they would have certainly arrested that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you ascertain from Vulevic how it is he became aware that it was a Skorpions or members of the people who were on the bus who had done the shooting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the spot, on that site, there were only the members of the reserve force there and somebody said that they had been shooting, but nobody actually saw who had done the shooting. Had somebody seen the shooting, then the person doing the shooting would have been arrested straightaway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, you said just now Vulevic, and this is at page 31, line 21, Vulevic, my commanding officer of the third platoon, said: "Boss, members of the third composition were shooting at the civilians, the ones that were supposed to be in the buses." Did you ascertain from Mr. Vulevic how he became aware of who was shooting at the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me just say Vulevic wasn't the commander of the 3rd Platoon. Vulevic was a komandir of the 3rd Platoon and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just reading to you what you said earlier. Maybe it's just that you were not answering the questions, why the record of your testimony is this. You said that Vulevic said that members -- that certain members were shooting the civilians. Did you find out from him why, on what basis he determined who was shooting the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just said, and I was following on from what you said, I said that Vulevic wasn't the commander of the 3rd Platoon but the komandir of the 3rd Platoon and that had -- he told me that members of the reserve force had shot but he didn't know who. If he had known who had been doing the shooting, he would have taken measures right away. That's what I said yesterday, that's what I said just a moment ago, and that's what I'm saying again now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you -- let's move on. Did you cause Mr. Vulevic to give a statement about what he witnessed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say with full responsibility no. It was in my interest as the senior officer that this should be established on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if Vulevic gave a statement in respect to these murders that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Vulevic did give several statements about this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That day, that day. Do you know of him giving a statement that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day he didn't make a statement of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, if --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, just a moment, please. Can I say this: On that day while I was present, on the territory of Podujevo, he did not give any statement. So while I was there on the Podujevo territory, he didn't give a statement. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 of the English, and I think we have to go to the top of page 2 in the Serbian version. I think this is, if my Cyrillic does not abandon me, this is the first paragraph on that page. And on to the first paragraph of the English, if we could scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said: "Members of the SAJ prevented members of the Skorpioni reserve unit, whose immediate commander, Boca, was at a meeting in the building of the Podujevo OUP at the time, from using fire-arms again." Did you say this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not say that, because if they had prevented the further use of fire-arms, they would have seen who was doing the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. So you signed to this, but you you didn't say it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Working Group didn't sign it either. None of them signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also refer to Boca as immediate commander. Did you tell them this, that's immediate commander of the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really can't remember now what I said at the time, and tell me what paragraph that's in so that I can read it for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think it's the last paragraph on the page in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it says members of the SAJ prevented the further use of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, and it refers to Boca or Boca as immediate commander of the Skorpion unit. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I still maintain that Boca was not an officer of the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So is your evidence that you didn't say this, that this record is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know from the context of my three-hour long interview who compiled all this. If I knew who wrote this and signed it -- well, I did sign it, that is my signature, but I really don't remember whether I actually said what it says here. I know that Mr. Medic was never the commander of the Skorpions on the territory of Serbia. He could only have been a member of the reserve force of the MUP of Serbia. I don't know if he was a commander anywhere for that matter. Mr. Trajkovic, before I set out to Prolom Banja to fetch them, he told me to report to Boca, but nothing more than that. Whether Trajkovic knew, I can't say. I don't know myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, you are not answering the questions. I just wanted to know if this record is correct, if you said this or if you didn't say that. And I understand your answer is that you didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in Serbian, I think we want the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "According to my information, the incident took place when somebody from the police provoked members of the Skorpioni reserve unit and because of the provocation they caused the incident in question." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really can't remember whether I said that then or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, do you recall now whether or not you learned on that day or received information about the circumstances in which these women and children were murdered?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What day? Could you just give me a date, please. You mean the 28th?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The 28th. While you were on the scene.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have said several times here that when I arrived on the scene, my 3rd Platoon commander Vulevic told me that the members who came by bus and were supposed to be in the bus shot at the civilians, but under what circumstances, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the next paragraph, and the third paragraph, that is just composed of one sentence, can you just read that aloud so we can get a translation of that directly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Who, which?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The third paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean "according to my knowledge"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The one after that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "According to my information, the commander of the SAJ Zivko Trajkovic." That one, that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. The one before that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "After the incident," is that the paragraph you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Until this event," that's how it starts. "According to my information," is that what it says, it's rather illegible. I'm not sure what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, the third paragraph on that page. And it is one sentence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the fourth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, the third.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "According to my information, the commander of the SAJ, Zivko Trajkovic, on the specified day at around 1400 hours was wounded and transferred to the hospital."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The paragraph immediately before that one.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Up until this event," is that the one you mean, that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The paragraph immediately before the one you started to read.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very well. "According to my information, this event came about because one of the policeman provoked members of the reserve unit of the Skorpion unit and because of that provocation they carried out the specific incident."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you read the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "After this event, following my order, on my orders" -- "after the incident, on my orders, members of the unit boarded the buses and returned to Prolom Banja."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you order the members of the unit to board the buses and return to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have repeated this a number of times. When I reached the scene and when I saw what had happened there, I told my members, the ones who were on the scene, that all the members of the reserve force should be returned to the buses and that they should wait to be sent back or returned to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In this statement and in your testimony to the Court, you said you ordered them. That's what I want. Did you order them on the buses and back to where you had brought them from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told the members of my unit, I ordered them, to send back all the Skorpion members on the buses and to send them to Prolom Banja, and if these -- if there were any members of the reserve force of the Serbia MUP, then certainly that order would have applied to them too because I, as a senior officer, can -- could order subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not asking you about the people that you referred to as members of your unit. I'm asking about the Skorpion members. And for the third time, I ask you again, it's simple, it's a simple question: Did you, as you said in the trial in Prokuplje and as you said in this statement, order the Skorpion members, order the Skorpion members, to board the buses and return to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To all those who were there, members of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. That is your answer. Did you cause any statements to be taken from any of the Skorpion members?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have told you that following this incident when I sent them back to Prolom Banja I left for Belgrade. The investigative authorities remained there and they were the ones who were supposed to conduct an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Could we just have a look at the Criminal Code for Serbia. I just want to ask you if you are aware of something.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we move to that document, could I ask that this document before the Court be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01590.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the previous document, Your Honours, 06118, that part which is the testimony, the record of the testimony of Mr. Simovic before the Prokuplje district court, if that part could be received as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we hesitated about that yesterday, Mr. Stamp, but in view of the further extent to which you've used it and the responses of the witness, I think it would be useful to have the statement in the record, so it too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01591.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Court Officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, before Mr. Stamp gets going with his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may seek an explanation. The 1591, P1591, that is the statement by Mr. Simovic that he provided at the trial on the 9th of October, 2001 before the Prokuplje court on pages 30, 31, and 32 of the transcript. Was my understanding correct, that's all I wanted to check?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you help us there, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I can in respect to the -- if it pleases Your Honours, I hope I can in respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood Exhibit P1591 as it now is that part of the transcript of the proceedings in the court in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That relates to the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think that is in the English the second part of the exhibit, pages 1 to 5. And I think in Serbian it starts at page 32. Pages 30 to 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that resolve the problem for you, Mr. Djurdjic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we also, I'm sorry, have the first page. The witness had looked at that to identify what the record was. That is the page indicating who the Judges were and how the Tribunal was set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want pages 1 and pages 30, 31, 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In Serbian. And it's pages 1 to 5 in English; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it's page 1, and I think the English is broken in two parts because there are separate translations done, so it's page 1 of the first part in English and page 1 to 5 of the second part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's suggested to me by the Court Officer that it may avoid confusion if at a convenient time today or tomorrow there was uploaded separately those pages in English and Serbian which you seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that is correct and if there is no difficulty with what we understand, that will be received. If there is a difficulty, the matter can be raised in court tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think we need to look at the -- or we might not. Are you aware that the Criminal Code of Serbia provides that any official who fails to report a crime or the perpetrators of a crime would be guilty of an offence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that this offence, this crime was reported. It was reported to the competent authorities, to the Podujevo OUP to take further steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you know that that is the legal position, that any official person who had any knowledge had a responsibility to make a report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think you also said that you informed Mr. Lukic, the head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I said that I informed the staff, not Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Who in the staff did you inform?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really can't remember now who was at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at D296.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is one of the daily report summaries of important events sent by the MUP staff to, among other people, the minister and also to Mr. Djordjevic. And this is dated the 29th of March, 1999. And if you look at the beginning there, the summary, it relates to security related events, incidents and information registered between 0600 hours on the 28th of March and 0600 hours on the 29th of March, 1999. That's the day of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page, please, in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's from Major Lukic and in paragraph 5, or section 5, in respect to serious crimes, there is no reference to this mass murder. Do you know why it is that the MUP staff did not record in its daily reporting this mass murder when they reported it to Mr. Djordjevic and to the minister? When they sent the report to Mr. Djordjevic and the minister? Do you know why it's not there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that on the 28th I reported to Podujevo OUP and informed the staff of this, and as to why it was not reported in this daily report, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. On the day of the incident when you reported it to Mr. Djordjevic, did he give you any instructions as to any further action you should take?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed the chief of the department that I had sent the unit back to Prolom Banja and that they should organise someone to receive them there, and because I could not reach Mr. Trajkovic, and I did not know where the other administrations were that I could inform, so that they could take measures against members of the reserve force. I only informed the chief of the department that I had sent them back and why I had sent them back, and then I went on to travel to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is not focused on the question I asked at all. Do you remember the question I asked you last?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you asked me whether I had informed the chief of department --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That I had sent the Skorpions back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. Please, please, listen to what I --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Then I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Listen to what I'm asking you. Did Mr. Djordjevic give you any instructions as to any further action you should take?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that point no. I just informed him of what had happened, that I had sent them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djordjevic give you any instructions as to any further action you should take at any point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told General Djordjevic on that occasion that I was going to Belgrade so that I couldn't take any steps in Belgrade, and there couldn't be any specific action that I should take, and he knew where I was going.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djordjevic at any point, give you any instructions as to any further action you should take?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In respect of what, this incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, in respect to what you reported to him.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Incidentally, Mr. Trajkovic said that when he got involved in the accident on the 27th, it was you who informed Mr. Djordjevic about the accident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I informed the chief of the department on the 28th that I was sending the reserve force back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking about that now. I'm only asking you now about the 27th. I think Mr. Trajkovic said that when Mr. Djordjevic was informed that he was injured, you agreed with Mr. Djordjevic to introduce the Skorpions, to take them over into Kosovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know what Mr. Trajkovic might have said and who he had a conversation with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just asking you -- forget about Mr. Trajkovic, what Mr. Trajkovic said. When Mr. Trajkovic was injured on the 27th, did you speak to Mr. Djordjevic about it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told you yesterday, and I repeat, on the 27th when he returned from the hospital in Pristina and from the staff, Mr. Trajkovic told me to go and fetch the reserve force, the MUP reserve force. I don't know what conversation you are referring to. Around 1700 hours on the 27th, I received instructions from Mr. Trajkovic to go to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you speak to Mr. Djordjevic on the 27th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already told you that I did not. Not on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. -- one moment. We had a former member of the Skorpions who testified before the trial and he said that when they returned to Banja Luka -- to Prolom Banja, no one questioned any of the Skorpions about the event in Podujevo. No one was arrested and taken into custody. No internal investigation was carried out. Were you aware that none of these things were done when the Skorpions, the perpetrators that you sent back went to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear about that, but on the same evening, on the 28th Prokuplje OUP inspectors were in Prolom Banja. Someone mentioned this to me. I can't remember who.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you about where police inspectors from Prokuplje might be and what they were doing. I'm asking you specifically about these Skorpions, the perpetrators of a mass murder that you sent back. Do you know that no one questioned them about this mass murder in Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know that while they were in Prolom Banja the perpetrators were known but nobody was arrested or taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
