utterances.text: I really don't. I told you that on the 28th I left for Belgrade and I have no further information as to what was happening with them, and I've repeated this on several occasions. After I left for Belgrade, I don't know what was happening with them because competent authorities took over and they were working on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is what I'm asking you. I'm asking you about the work of the competent authorities. You sent back these mass murderers with their weapons without taking even a statement. Do you know that while they were in Prolom Banja, there was no investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that measures were taken to conduct all investigative measures, but after I left for Belgrade, I don't know what transpired nor could I have any impact on the course of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When did you return to Kosovo from Belgrade? How many days after the 28th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that I don't remember exactly on what date, but it was immediately following the funeral that I returned to Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At some time around the 29th, 30th, 31st March?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you went to Kosovo Polje where the SAJ had established its base when you returned to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, on that occasion I went to Gracanica where the forward command post of the Pristina SAJ was because the NATO air-strikes had begun, and we could not remain at the base in Ajvalija. I was informed there that the new base of the SAJ was in Kosovo Polje, and then I went to Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, is it correct that sometime in about -- I think this is your evidence, so just tell me yes or no -- sometime in about the middle of April or after the 15th or 16th of April the Skorpions were bused, were taken back to the SAJ base, this time at Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I said that in late April they arrived and the then-Commander Trajkovic then took over control of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Couldn't it be on or about the 15th -- sorry, on or about the 18th of April? Could that qualify as an approximate time when the Skorpions returned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I said it was in late April, the end of April, that could be the 28th, the 29th, or the 30th. Not the 18th. The end of the month, not mid-month.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Stoparic he said that he was re-recruited on the 15th or 16th, and a couple of days later he was taken to Kosovo Polje where Mr. Trajkovic had his headquarters in a large house. Did Mr. Trajkovic have headquarters in a house in Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the SAJ headquarters or staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And he said that when he and the remainder of the Skorpions returned there, you were still one of Mr. Trajkovic deputies, or you were still commander of the Belgrade SAJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was never deputy commander to Commander Trajkovic. I was never his deputy. I was never the deputy to Commander Trajkovic. I was the commander of the Belgrade SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Stoparic testified that -- well, before we get to that, the Skorpions who rejoined you in late April, as you say, were they assigned to both of the SAJ units at Belgrade and the Pristina unit, or were they assigned to only one?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already said, when Mr. Trajkovic took them over, members of the reserve force were sent or were divided, and one group was sent to the Pristina SAJ and the other group to the Belgrade SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic also testified that all of the men but one who shot these civilian women and children were returned armed and given high-powered weapons and put on their command again. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know what Stoparic or Stoparevic, as you call him, I don't know who the man is who you are referring to, what statement he gave. I said when they were returned at the end of April, when they were taken over by Mr. Trajkovic, that they were divided, the SAJ in Pristina and the SAJ in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like us and the witness to be shown parts of the statement by the witness referred to by Mr. Stamp. Now, the last piece of interpretation I received about these weapons, and I don't know what strength the weapons were and everything else, I don't know that this is mentioned and the name Stoparic mentioned, so I think it would be a good idea if we were to see what it is that Stoparic is saying so that we can read it and then we can go on to asking the witness questions and see whether it's right or wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You do need, at least, to give a reference if you are quoting from statements so that Mr. Djurdjic can follow you up, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Page 2844, lines -- well, I'll just read the answer, line 22 to 25. Answer of Mr. Stoparic: "First let me correct you. We were not redeployed to Podujevo but rather to Kosovo Polje. Of the man that I claimed have taken part in the execution of a civilian, only Cvjetan Sasa didn't return. All the rest returned."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anyway, Witness, forget Stoparic. The question is this: Do you know at the time of the redeployment of any measures that had been taken to weed out, so to speak, or purge, or discover those persons who were responsible for the massacre?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Commander Trajkovic said, told me and Commander Stalevic, that he would again ask the minister that the reserve MUP composition be assigned to us but in a sifted version. What he meant, I don't know, but all I know is that none of the reserve forces could come and be part of the reserve forces without being checked out, their criminal records checked out and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So are you saying that you know that their criminal records were checked out? You know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's the duty of the police, when they engage somebody to become a member of the reserve force, they have to check that person out. That's their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anyway, you are telling me about what is supposed to happen. I'm asking you if you know if that happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They couldn't have been engaged in the reserve force in the first place without having been checked out by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Back to the question. Do you know of any measures that had been taken by late April when the Skorpions returned to be re-engaged with the SAJ, to weed out those who had committed the crime at Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew that the procedure was underway, but nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I take it that at that time you didn't know whether or not you were re-engaging mass murderers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know the members of the reserve force by name. They were returned as the reserve force of the MUP attached to the SAJ, and they were supposed to come previously having been checked out by the police. It was the police that were supposed to have done the checks. We don't select MUP reservists. They are assigned to us. The SAJ does not have a reserve force, and I've said that any number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you are saying things which are not related to my question. Having not done anything or having -- or not knowing what steps had been taken, you were re-engaging persons who -- that you did not know whether or not they had committed crimes; is that true? When I say crimes, committed the crime at Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's not true that I didn't undertake anything. When that unfortunate event took place, I reported it to Podujevo. I informed the staff about it and the OUP of Podujevo informed the investigating judge and the proceedings went on from there, so I don't make the decision about whether the reserve force would be attached to me or not. It comes from a proposal from Commander Trajkovic and the people that were -- the reserve force added on to us attached to us were returned, according to Mr. Trajkovic, that they had been checked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said yesterday that, and I'll find it to read it. At page 13594, page 18 [sic], and this is in respect to these Skorpion members or members of the reserve force that came back to Kosovo Polje: "Some of them were assigned to the SAJ in Belgrade and some to the SAJ in Pristina. Once they were attached to my unit, and this was in Kosovo Polje, I organised a meeting with these men. I hadn't -- I didn't -- I didn't identify any of them as being the participant in the incident in Podujevo." On what basis, Mr. Simovic, could you identify or not identify any of these men as participants in the murder, if you didn't follow the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that I didn't recognise anybody who was on the scene in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. I just read what you said.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said when Commander Trajkovic took them over in Kosovo Polje and when a certain number attached to me, and when I talked to them, that I didn't recognise anybody from the scene in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's what you say now. But the record indicates that you didn't identify any of them as being a participant in the incident in Podujevo. So the question is: On what basis could you determine who was a participant and who was not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say again, I didn't recognise anybody from the scene as having been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Simovic, I represent to you that the record is a record of what you said yesterday, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at D441. This is the on-site investigation report. Could we move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: One page in Serbian, is it, or two pages? Did you see this on-site report, on-site investigation report before you reincorporated these men on your command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In one paragraph -- well, you said you haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter 1841.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, Mr. Simovic, I want to recall for the time being is the on-site investigation report in this massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry, Defence 65 ter. This is a document on the Defence list which we got yesterday. And I think I'm told that it should be referred to at this point in time by the e-court ID, identification number, which is D003-1454 in English and D003-1452 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is ruling to conduct an investigation and to order the detention of suspects by the investigating Judge Mijat Bajovic of the Prokuplje district court, and it's dated the 24th of May, 1999. This was more than -- well, approximately a month after the Skorpions are re-engaged. And if you look at it in the ruling it relates to Sasa Cvjetan and Dejan Demirovic, and you can see that they were taken into custody on the 21st of May, 1999. Did you know that that is when these men were arrested, these two men were arrested?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not know of the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to the charge section where it says "For" and then "Suspect Sasa Cvjetan," it reads: "Reasonable grounds suspect that on the 28th of March, 1999 in Podujevo, as a member of the reserve force of the SAJ (special anti-terrorist unit) with premeditated intent, while participating in operative processing of the terrain, killed several persons..." Do you know on what basis did the investigating magistrate refer to Cvjetan as a member of the reserve force of the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know. Perhaps it's Cvjetan's statement. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you know that this is done, this order is issued before the magistrate interviews the witness -- interviews the accused, don't you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know nothing about that -- anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the next page in respect to Dejan Demirovic, he is also described -- and we only need to move in English forward to the next page. He is also described as a member of the reserve force of the SAJ. I take it you don't know about that either?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you aware -- well, if you go back to the first page, we can see that they were arrested on the 21st of May, 1999. I think we have pointed that out before, so maybe I could move to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01592.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could look at document B/C/S e-court ID D003-1452. English D003-1454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That seems to be the reference, Mr. Stamp, to the document that has just become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance? If the other document is under a D number, then it is 003-1431.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what the Prosecutor had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are better at reading his mind than I am, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in English it's D003-1433.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While that is coming up, Mr. Trajkovic testified that for some reason this massacre received a lot of attention in the press in Serbia. Do you recall that happening in 1999 during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. Who said that, did you say? I did not understand the name, who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It doesn't matter who said it. Do you recall that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene. In the interpretation it said that some -- that a man called Cekovic [phoen] said something to the media. That's what the witness heard and that's what I heard, but in the transcript the name is quite different as you can see here. So through our headsets we heard Mr. Cekovic, that it was Mr. Cekovic who said what Mr. Stamp said about the public information media.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, I'll ask the question without referring to the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During the war in May, did this massacre become a feature of some notoriety in the media in Serbia and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember the note in the media, but I can't remember the date because in May I was elsewhere. I was in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at this document quickly. This is a criminal report charging Mr. Cvjetan and Mr. Demirovic. Your copy is probably not the most legible, but if we look at the -- at paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While you are sorting that out, Mr. Stamp, yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's a document which is to be found in hard copy. It exists in hard copy, so it is number 5, document number 5, and perhaps the witness could be provided with a hard copy to look at. It might be easier for the witness to see if in front of him rather than looking at the screen and e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would that help, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But anyway, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Found it, Mr. Simovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's the criminal report against these two men, Dejan Demirovic and Sasa Cvjetan. On the 23rd of May, 1999. If we go to the last page, you'll see that it was signed by Captains Klikovac and Oparnica, and they were from the OUP Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know which OUP they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you have the document in front of you. If you go to the first page, you will see who the document is from.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It doesn't say where they were from here. It just says Dusko -- it just says Captains Dusko Klikovac and Milos Oparnica, authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Go to the first page. It was sent by the department of the interior of Podujevo, 23rd of May. KU Number 6599 is the serial number.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it refers to both of them, and this is the third paragraph of section 2, that: "Sasa Cvjetan and Dejan Demirovic, with several other unidentified perpetrators, as members of the reserve force of the SAJ." Why would these two captains in the Podujevo OUP characterise them as members of the reserve force of the SAJ; do you know why?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know, and I repeat again, SAJ did not have its own reserve force, nor did it ever have one. We received our reserve forces from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia only as an attachment, but we didn't have an SAJ reserve force. The SAJ never had a reserve force of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we go back to the last page quickly. We'll see that the -- this is -- again I remind you of a date. This is late May, two months after the incident. This is the police report charging two people, and you see the attachments, on-site investigation report, KR Number 21 of 1999, which is the on-site investigation report of one page, which I showed you five minutes ago; written statements by the reported persons, that is the two accused; decision on remand in custody; a record of a search of Sasa Cvjetan; forensic documentation of the scene. Upon until that time they hadn't taken any statements from any of your policemen, any of the Skorpions except these two persons who are now being arrested. Were you aware of that? Two months later these are the state of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know how the competent authorities organised this work. They did the best they could and I really don't know because I didn't take part in the identification and other matters. I was in charge of my unit, and this was conducted by the investigating judge in Prokuplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you aware that as a result of this, that Cvjetan and Demirovic, although they were arrested, they were released within ten days? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When they were tried, when you testified at the trial in Prokuplje in 2003, they had been re-arrested, and this was after this Tribunal became involved, at least at the trial. They had been re-arrested for that trial; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I became aware of that when I was summonsed by the Court to appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you are aware of that that even at that stage because of the investigation that had proceeded, the case against these men had to be dismissed and to be recommenced two years later in Belgrade; are you aware of that -- or withdrawn, I'm not sure how long after. This case in Prokuplje had to be dismissed and was later recommenced in Belgrade; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that. All I know is that they were convicted, sentenced, and that I'm glad that they were actually meted out a decision or actually a punishment that they deserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document before the Court, I tender it and ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01593.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second adjournment now and resume at 6.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, were you deployed with the SAJ in Eastern Slavonia in the period 1991 to 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you deployed as a policeman in Croatia at any time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said yesterday at -- and I'm moving on to something else -- at 13594, if I could quote you, in respect to these reservists: "What is important was that they had all served in the army because there was a requirement for all members of these reserve force. They would have had to serve in the army. And based on what military specialty they had served in while they were in the army, they would be used in order to establish groups or teams that were -- that would be capable of carrying out certain tasks." Would the requirement, what you said was the important requirement that they had served in the army, did that apply to every one of these Skorpion, these members of the units, the Skorpion unit, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that every member of the reserve force of the MUP in order to qualify to become a member of the reserve MUP force would have had to serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Right. If we look at the Law on Internal Affairs for the Republic of Serbia. That's P66, Article 27, I think there's a provision for that. If you go just very quickly to remind us of what the law says. While it's coming up, can you answer me precisely, did you, of your own knowledge, become aware that the members of this unit, which I refer to, the Skorpion, had -- were members of the army had done their military service, or are you assuming this because this was a requirement of the law?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The police administration had to comply with the legal provisions, and members of the reserve MUP forces had to have served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So basically you assume this on the basis of the legal requirements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is understood that they would have served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that's Article 27, providing: "In case of an imminent threat of war or war, the Ministry of the Interior shall be brought up to strength with conscripts to the reserve force of the ministry." There's a slight error in that translation. But that is the relevant legal provision, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only conscripts may be deployed, those who also meet the legal requirements to work in the Ministry of the Interior. In other words, those who have served in the army can be actually engaged to work in the reserve force of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you aware that many of these members of the Skorpions had no military service?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I only knew that the police administration had to comply with the procedure whereby the reserve MUP force members had to have served in the army. Whether the police administration actually did comply with this legal provision, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. We've had evidence on this, the question is slightly different, not what ought to have been done. We understand that the law is that for war time engagement of a reservist of the MUP, they would have to be conscripts and pass other requirements. I am asking you now, when these men were re-engaged to you at Kosovo Polje, were you aware or did you become aware that many of them were not conscripts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Kosovo Polje they were received by Commander Trajkovic, and he actually assigned them to the Pristina SAJ and to my unit. I did not question the commander's decision and I didn't know that there were among them those who were not conscripts, because in order to qualify to become a member of the reserve force of the MUP, they would have had to serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic testified that as much as 50 per cent of the 120 Skorpion members had no previous combat experience. Some didn't even know how to handle weapons. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know what Mr. Stoparic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you aware that approximately 50 per cent of the Skorpions had no combat experience, some couldn't even handle weapons properly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I knew was that they were members of the reserve force and that the requirement was for them to have served in the army and if they hadn't, then that was an omission committed by the police administration and not an error on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm just asking about what you knew at the time. I'm not saying that you made an error.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't know at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We had the testimony of General Aleksandar Vasiljevic who said that he asked for a check to be made of who these Skorpions were, and the report he got back was that "there were many persons with criminal records and that they had a general reputation of being criminals. There were many criminal types in their ranks. They were problematic people." That's quoting him. During the war that never came to your attention, that you were co-mingling with -- well, that these Skorpions that were engaged with you included persons who were criminals or criminal types?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What General Vasiljevic said, I don't know. What I do know is that the member of the reserve MUP force could not be admitted as a member of the reserve force unless they went through background checks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate the reference where Mr. Vasiljevic said this, that he actually said this of members of the reserve MUP force who were attached to the SAJ unit, and could he please tell us where this reference is coming from, which part of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What I put was that General Vasiljevic said he made a check on the Skorpions who were attached to the MUP and that the Skorpions included persons who were criminals and criminal types, and this is 5666 and 5667 of the record. Those are transcript pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovic [sic] said at 5666 from lines 13: What is stated in the report was that the group was headed by Slobodan Medic and that the group he organised [indiscernible] himself comprised 120 to 150 people, that there were practically two groups who went to Kosovo, one that was organised by Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, at the initiative of Mrgan Denanovic [phoen] who in 1991 had been appointed as [indiscernible] Slavonia minister of defence, and that the other group was organised and led by Dalibor Novakovic. The report also said that in essence, these persons had experience in the battle-field in the former Yugoslavia, that among them there were persons who had criminal records, but no names are named, that they had returned to Kosovo a couple of days earlier. So since we are there, did you know of another group of reservists that were organised around somebody by the name of Dalibor Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. -- General Vasiljevic said, among the persons, there were many persons who had criminal records. You weren't aware -- well, were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Vasiljevic said, but I know that one could not become a member of the reserve force in the MUP if that person had a criminal record, and without background checks. So they would have to be a conscript to have served in the army, and in order to become a member of the reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Later on at page 5667, Mr. Vasiljevic was asked: "Briefly, in maybe a sentence or two, did your operative report indicate what the reputation was in respect to what they had been up to in the battle-fields in the former Yugoslavia? "A. I don't know specifically what they had done there. I know they were paid as an organised group in the so-called Bihac operation. Simply there were some MUP units, JSO to be more precise, in that area. The general classification was that there were criminal types in their ranks, problematic people, which was written in the dossiers of those people who had returned from the battle-fields." That is Mr. Vasiljevic's testimony. Are you aware that this was the sort of people that you were recruiting into the police force?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying again I don't know what Mr. Vasiljevic said. I don't understand this. All I can say, and I have to repeat it, is that every member of the reserve force in the MUP had to be a conscript, and they had to not have a criminal record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but to recruit police officers, don't you also check their backgrounds to see what their reputation is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reserve forces of the MUP, the people who actually applied to become members were being checked by the police administration in charge of that. As for members of the SAJ, I personally conducted the background checks and all the other necessary checks. An active member of the SAJ could become an active member only if he or she was already an employee of the Ministry of the Interior and had a good record as an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, one of the better workers. And of course, they had also had to qualify, they had to meet all the requirements for admittance into the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You remember we were speaking earlier about the charges against Demirovic and Cvjetan, they were two people who were charged in 2002 and 2003, but I represent to you, Mr. Simovic, that there were more than two people who were shooting during the incident. And I'd like to show you the last indictment, the 2008 indictment, against some of the remaining people who have now been charged in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at document 06116.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you aware that in the latter part of 2007 or 2008 four other persons were charged in respect to this massacre in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard it in the media, and I was pleased that the investigation uncovered the other participants in this massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could pause there to see where we are at. This is an indictment of the 14th of April, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The first person charged --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to the bottom in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- is a Zeljko Djukic, and if we could move on in English to look at the second person charged, Dragan Medic. We'll see in his description in this indictment, he had no military service, no military record, no criminal record. So you note here that we have here somebody with no military service at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I see that now, and that was an omission by the police administration unit that mobilised these reserve force members.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The third person charged, Dragan Borojevic, you could look at this one, and if you could just read -- just read to yourself -- the criminal record dating back to before 1996.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It seems that on the -- if we move to the next page in English so that we could look at it. It seems that prior -- it seems that on the 25th of November, 1996, he was sentenced to imprisonment for extortion, and we can see that prior to that he was also sentenced imprisonment for unauthorised possession of weapons. So how is it that an interested person like General Vasiljevic could make one inquiry for these people to be checked out and he could immediately and quickly receive information that this group was composed of many criminal and criminal types, yet you didn't know about that, Mr. Trajkovic didn't know about that, Mr. Djordjevic didn't know about that? All you senior policemen didn't know about it, yet Mr. Vasiljevic on one inquiry could discover it. Could you explain that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The police administration was duty-bound to do a background check on each individual and it did so. How this omission occurred, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at the next one, Miodrag Solaja. You see that he has a criminal record as well, two or three offences here for which he was sentenced imprisonment. They were subsequent to 1999, but this is the type of persons that you are working with, Mr. Simovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not co-operate with them. The reserve forces of the Republic of Serbia MUP was taken over by Trajkovic, and he assigned it to the special units of the SAJ Pristina and SAJ Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at the judgement against Sasa Cvjetan, we would also see that he was a criminal, notwithstanding that his offence, his other offence, apart from the massacre that he was convicted of, was committed subsequent to the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is P40, and it's on the first page, and that is the judgement against Sasa Cvjetan in the Belgrade court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you know about that conviction? Or maybe we should just look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you bring P40 before the Court. And go to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at the judgement, so that is the part on the second heading. Crimes in 2001, 2004. This is after he had been released because the Podujevo massacre wasn't investigated, he still continued along a criminal career. You see that? Mr. Simovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you know -- you know Boca, Slobodan Medic, he is serving a 40-year term for another massacre that was committed in the mid-1990s, about five years before the Podujevo incident in Bosnia, where he and some other of his Skorpion members lined up a group of boys and young men and executed them? You know that? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learned of that in the media, also during the trial of Slobodan Milosevic before this Tribunal. I know that some footage was shown of this crime committed by the Skorpion unit in Bosnia. That was the first time that I heard of it. And as for Mr. Medic, I've already told you, I told you yesterday, that I met him for the first time and saw him for the first time when I went to Prolom Banja when Mr. Zivko Trajkovic told me that he would be there. Before Podujevo, I had never seen Mr. Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again I ask you, Mr. Simovic, you see, any time we see in the record of these persons, almost all of these records show the character of these persons who were incorporated to the police and given high-powered weapons and put in positions where they are amongst civilians. This is what we are seeing. General Vasiljevic upon hearing about them made an inquiry and he learned that these were criminals who had been incorporated in the police. How is it, Mr. Djordjevic, who was responsible or participated in engaging them in the police force did not know about these men? You are a senior policeman. Tell us, how could it have escaped him in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I state again, reception into the MUP, there's special department in the police administration dealing with that. And it was up to them to take people in. And we read an article of the Law on Internal Affairs. Only those people who had completed their military service and who didn't have a criminal police file could be admitted. So I really don't know what you are asking, how this was done, because I didn't do it. I don't know why that hadn't been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could look at 06113. Before we do that, Your Honour, could the document before the one on e-court now, 06116, be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01594.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could now look at 06113.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a military document. I think earlier that you did your military service. Are you familiar with documents like this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't do my military service, and this is the first time that I see a document of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the 16th of May supplement to a report from the 3rd Army security department. And in the penultimate paragraph -- can you read it? It says that: "Major-General verified information Major-General Djakovic, operative officer in command of the 3rd Army, recognised in this group a certain Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, and asked what sort of task had brought him there. To which the other replied that he had come under the order of the MUP General Roda." Who is normally referred to as -- who is General Roda? Who is that referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before. This is the first time I'm looking at it. Now, what Mr. Djakovic wrote here, I really can't comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who is MUP General Roda, that's all I'm asking now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I can tell you all the MUP generals, give you their names, their first name and last name, but I don't know their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You don't know that General Djordjevic is referred to as General Roda, or that Roda is his nickname or Radja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never addressed him by his nickname. I was a professional myself and I always addressed my superiors by rank or position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but this document refers to Boca speaking. Boca is a different quality of person. Do you know what General Djordjevic's nickname was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already said, as far as my superior officers are concerned, I always addressed them by name and surname or by rank. As to nicknames, I know that Commander Trajkovic was Zile because we were close, but as for the others, I really don't know. They might have any one of thousands of nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you present when the Skorpions received their weapons in Prolom Banja on the 27th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I want to move on from this document but I wouldn't tender it. I would just ask that it be marked since it was shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01595 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the last document that I'd like to show you, Mr. Simovic, is 06111. This is a report to the investigation department of the district court of Prokuplje dated the 11th of March, 2002. I can just indicate that on the English translation, there's an error in that the date is not included in the top left-hand column as it is in the original in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it is in respect to a request from the district court, and if we just move to the end of the document to see who it's from, it's from the chief of administration, Major-General Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Page 2 in the B/C/S, page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we go back to page 2 -- the first page, we see that Major Knezevic is from the administration for prevention of organised crime, and it says: "The administration for prevention of organised crime acted upon your request to collect the required information in order to successfully conduct an investigation against the accused persons, Sasa Cvjetan and Dejan Demirovic for a criminal offence of war crimes against the civilian population under Article 142." And in the first bullet point it says: "Accused Cvjetan and Demirovic were members of the Skorpion units." And the second bullet points it says: "The Skorpions was founded as a volunteer unit of 128 members." Was it lawful to incorporate volunteers into the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Volunteers were never incorporated into the police, nor could somebody volunteer to join up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was not lawful?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was not lawful?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reserve force was recruited into the police by the department for the reserve force in the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you look at the second page in English, I think it's the bottom of the first page in B/C/S, it says: "On the 25th of March, 1999, the Skorpions unit was transferred to the reserve formations of the MUP SAJ with the approval of Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic..."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about this piece of information. I'm not aware of it, and this is the first time that I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But this is a document emanating from the MUP; you would at least agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know who wrote this document, but as I say, this is the first time that I'm hearing about this. I know that the police administration, or rather, the department of the reserve force, took in members of the reserve force into MUP. Admitted members of the reserve force into MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this police report be received in evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have two objections. The first is that this document has nothing to do with this witness. He did not draft it, nor did he take part in its drafting, nor does he know anything about this document. And the second point is this, the document has a number of pages and everything that is contained in this document and which is on e-court is not a component part of the document to which Mr. Stamp refers. But if you wish, I can explain why or we can carry on tomorrow morning in view of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe I could check and sort out whatever it is overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we'll leave it overnight, and if you want to pursue that, do so. And the matter can be taken up again when we resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must adjourn overnight now to resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. The Court Officer will assist you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st of April, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.
